title: Seventh Word Conclusion Counsel On Prayer Avoiding Major Sins Listening To The Quran And Supplication

questions.question: What is the first main request made to Allah at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: It asks Allah to fill hearts with the light of faith and the Qur’an.

questions.question: In the prayer, what kind of richness is asked for?
questions.answer: A richness that comes from recognizing one’s need for Allah.

questions.question: What kind of poverty is the speaker asking to be protected from?
questions.answer: The poverty that comes from acting as if one has no need of Allah.

questions.question: What does the prayer say about human strength and power?
questions.answer: It rejects depending on human ability and seeks refuge in Allah’s ability and power instead.

questions.question: What relationship to Allah is requested through the phrase about trust?
questions.answer: The prayer asks to be among those who rely on Allah.

questions.question: What danger is being avoided in the request not to be left to ourselves?
questions.answer: The danger of being abandoned to one’s own weak self.

questions.question: Besides asking for personal mercy, who else is included in the supplication for mercy?
questions.answer: All believing men and women.

questions.question: How is Prophet Muhammad described in relation to servanthood and prophethood?
questions.answer: He is described as Allah’s servant and prophet.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Prophet Muhammad’s closeness to Allah?
questions.answer: He is presented as beloved, chosen, and near to Allah.

questions.question: What do the titles connected to guidance and proof show about the Prophet’s role?
questions.answer: They show that he guides people and conveys clear evidence of truth.

questions.question: What do the titles about signs, names, and teaching show about his mission?
questions.answer: They show that he explains Allah’s signs, makes Allah’s names known, and teaches Allah’s servants.

questions.question: How is Prophet Muhammad connected to mercy in this prayer?
questions.answer: He is described as a model of mercy and as the messenger sent as mercy to all worlds.

questions.question: Which groups are included after blessings are asked for the Prophet himself?
questions.answer: His family, his companions, his brother prophets and messengers, the near angels, and the righteous servants of Allah.

questions.question: What does the ending word “Amen” express in this supplication?
questions.answer: It expresses a hopeful affirmation, asking Allah to accept the prayer.

questions.question: What is the overall form of the marked passage: argument, story, or supplication?
questions.answer: It is a supplication.

questions.question: What two sources of inner illumination are mentioned together in the opening line?
questions.answer: Faith and the Qur’an.

questions.question: How does the prayer connect true wealth with a servant’s condition before Allah?
questions.answer: It treats awareness of need before Allah as real wealth.

questions.question: How does the prayer treat self-sufficiency apart from Allah?
questions.answer: It presents that attitude as a kind of poverty.

questions.question: What shift happens after the request about need and dependence?
questions.answer: The prayer moves from asking for help with dependence to praising and sending blessings on the Prophet.

questions.question: What is being renounced when the speaker says they are free of their own power?
questions.answer: Trust in personal strength and control.

questions.question: What is being embraced when refuge is sought in Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Dependence on Allah’s support and protection.

questions.question: Why does the prayer ask not to be entrusted to ourselves?
questions.answer: Because the self is not a safe or sufficient guide.

questions.question: What does the request for protection imply about Allah?
questions.answer: It implies that Allah is the true guardian and protector.

questions.question: In the long praise section, what do the many titles of the Prophet mainly do?
questions.answer: They highlight the greatness of his mission and his special rank.

questions.question: How is the Prophet linked to Allah’s guidance in the passage?
questions.answer: He is described as a shining means through which guidance reaches creation.

questions.question: How is the Prophet linked to Allah’s signs and names?
questions.answer: He is shown as one who explains divine signs and makes divine names known to people.

questions.question: What does the phrase about being sent to all worlds show about the scope of his mission?
questions.answer: It shows that his mercy and message are universal, not limited to one group.

questions.question: What balance appears in the passage between personal needs and the wider believing community?
questions.answer: The prayer asks for help for the speaker but also includes believers, the Prophet’s community, and other honored servants of Allah.

questions.question: What spiritual problem is answered by the request for hearts to be lit?
questions.answer: The problem of inner darkness and lack of spiritual clarity.

questions.question: Why would needing Allah be described as a form of enrichment?
questions.answer: Because recognizing dependence on Allah gives a person spiritual strength and right orientation.

questions.question: Why would thinking oneself independent of Allah be described as impoverishing?
questions.answer: Because it cuts a person off from the true source of help and honor.

questions.question: What attitude toward human ability is being taught in the line about our own strength and power?
questions.answer: Humility about human limits.

questions.question: What practical spiritual quality is being asked for in the request to be among those who trust Allah?
questions.answer: Steady reliance on Allah.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the human self from the request not to be left to it?
questions.answer: It can fail, mislead, and cannot safely carry a person on its own.

questions.question: What does the prayer suggest about the connection between protection and mercy?
questions.answer: Both are sought from Allah as essential needs for human well-being.

questions.question: Why does the prayer mention believing men and women, not just the speaker?
questions.answer: It teaches concern for the whole community of believers.

questions.question: What does calling the Prophet both servant and prophet show?
questions.answer: It joins his complete devotion to Allah with his role of delivering revelation.

questions.question: What is suggested by calling him a means through which Allah’s proof is expressed?
questions.answer: That his message makes truth clear and leaves people with no excuse.

questions.question: What is suggested by calling him an interpreter of divine signs?
questions.answer: That he explains revelation and the meanings of Allah’s signs to people.

questions.question: What does calling him a mirror of divine beauty suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that his life and mission reflect Allah’s qualities in a created form.

questions.question: How does the passage present the Prophet’s place among created beings?
questions.answer: It presents him as highly honored and distinguished among them.

questions.question: What final tone does the prayer end with?
questions.answer: A tone of hope, reverence, and submission.

questions.question: According to the prayer, what brings light to the heart?
questions.answer: Belief and the Qur’an, by Allah’s permission.

questions.question: Which is treated as better: feeling need for Allah or feeling independent from Him?
questions.answer: Feeling need for Allah.

questions.question: What contrast is made between these two conditions?
questions.answer: Neediness toward Allah is treated as richness, while independence from Him is treated as poverty.

questions.question: What two things of our own are set aside in the prayer?
questions.answer: Our own power and our own strength.

questions.question: In place of those, what two things are sought from Allah?
questions.answer: Allah’s power and Allah’s strength.

questions.question: What group does the prayer ask to be placed among?
questions.answer: Those who trust in Allah.

questions.question: What personal condition does the speaker ask Allah not to leave them in?
questions.answer: Being left to themselves.

questions.question: Name two broad blessings requested before the salawat on the Prophet begins.
questions.answer: Protection and mercy.

questions.question: What two groups of believers are specifically mentioned in the request for mercy?
questions.answer: Believing men and believing women.

questions.question: What do the many honorific descriptions of the Prophet emphasize more than anything else?
questions.answer: His noble station and many-sided service in conveying guidance.

questions.question: According to the passage, how is the Prophet related to Allah’s servants?
questions.answer: He teaches them.

questions.question: According to the passage, how is the Prophet related to Allah’s signs?
questions.answer: He explains them.

questions.question: Who are included with the Prophet in the prayer for blessings after his family and companions?
questions.answer: Other prophets and messengers, the angels close to Allah, and righteous servants.

questions.question: What is the function of the final “Amen” in the passage?
questions.answer: It seals the supplication with a request for acceptance.

questions.question: What is being asked for the heart rather than for the body or wealth?
questions.answer: Spiritual light.

questions.question: From what two things does that light come in the prayer?
questions.answer: From faith and the Qur’an.

questions.question: How does the prayer redefine what it means to be rich?
questions.answer: It defines richness as needing Allah.

questions.question: How does the prayer redefine what it means to be poor?
questions.answer: It defines poverty as living with a sense of independence from Allah.

questions.question: What kind of self-understanding is taught by declaring freedom from our own power?
questions.answer: A self-understanding based on weakness and dependence before Allah.

questions.question: What is the positive alternative to relying on oneself in this passage?
questions.answer: Taking shelter in Allah’s power and trusting Him.

questions.question: What does the request for divine protection tell us about human vulnerability?
questions.answer: It shows that human beings need Allah’s guarding care.

questions.question: How does the prayer move from the individual to the community?
questions.answer: It begins with “our” needs and then asks mercy for all believing men and women.

questions.question: What title shows the Prophet’s role in communicating Allah’s message in understandable form?
questions.answer: He is described as one who interprets Allah’s signs.

questions.question: What title shows the Prophet’s role in educating people in religion?
questions.answer: He is described as the teacher of Allah’s servants.

questions.question: What title shows the Prophet’s special place in relation to mercy for creation?
questions.answer: He is described as the messenger sent as mercy to all worlds.

questions.question: How does the prayer portray the Prophet’s connection to divine guidance?
questions.answer: It portrays him as a radiant source through which guidance shines.

questions.question: Which unseen beings are directly included in the closing blessings?
questions.answer: The angels near to Allah.

questions.question: What does the structure of the whole passage show about proper adab in du‘a?
questions.answer: It shows asking Allah directly, admitting need, seeking mercy, and sending blessings on the Prophet.

questions.question: What is the opening request of the marked passage concerned with: outer success or inner guidance?
questions.answer: Inner guidance.

questions.question: What image is used for that guidance in the opening line?
questions.answer: Light.

questions.question: What paradox appears in the line about enrichment and poverty?
questions.answer: Need for Allah is called richness, while claimed independence from Him is called poverty.

questions.question: What spiritual lesson comes from asking not to be made independent of Allah?
questions.answer: A believer should never see himself as self-sufficient before Allah.

questions.question: What confession is made about human power in the middle of the prayer?
questions.answer: That our own power and strength are not what we should rely on.

questions.question: What replacement for self-reliance does the prayer teach?
questions.answer: Seeking shelter in Allah’s power and strength.

questions.question: What ongoing quality of faith is requested by asking to be made among those who trust Allah?
questions.answer: Continual reliance on Allah.

questions.question: Why is the request not to be left to ourselves so important in the logic of the prayer?
questions.answer: Because all safety, steadiness, and success are understood to come from Allah, not the isolated self.

questions.question: What does the prayer reveal about the scope of mercy a believer should ask for?
questions.answer: It should include oneself and the whole body of believing men and women.

questions.question: In the praise of the Prophet, what pattern do the many titles create?
questions.answer: They create a layered portrait of his honor, beauty, guidance, teaching, and mercy.

questions.question: Which descriptions show that the Prophet helps people know Allah better?
questions.answer: The ones presenting him as making Allah’s names known, explaining the signs, and conveying what pleases Allah.

questions.question: Which description shows that the Prophet’s mission reaches beyond one nation?
questions.answer: The description that he was sent as mercy to all worlds.

questions.question: What other honored groups receive blessings after the Prophet in this passage?
questions.answer: His family, companions, fellow prophets and messengers, the near angels, and righteous servants.

questions.question: How would you summarize the main themes of the whole marked passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: It is a prayer for faith, dependence on Allah, protection, mercy, and blessings upon the Prophet and the righteous.
